text:
Lime.

The rain lashed against the precinct windows, mirroring the storm brewing in Detective Howard’s chest. He stared at the file on his desk, the paper trembling slightly in his grip. It wasn't just evidence; it was a betrayal wrapped in the guise of duty. His partner, Marcus, the man who had pulled him from a burning car and shared a beer every Friday for twenty years, was the suspect.

Howard’s hand hovered over the phone. To call it in was to destroy Marcus. To ignore it was to destroy himself. The weight of the badge felt heavier than ever, pressing down on his shoulders. He looked at the framed photo on his desk—him and Marcus, smiling, arms around each other’s shoulders. Now, that smile looked like a mask. The conflict wasn't just about the law; it was about the man he thought he knew. Every second he delayed, the tension in the room thickened, suffocating him. He had to choose: loyalty or justice. And as the clock ticked toward his retirement, Howard realized that whichever choice he made, the man he was would cease to exist.
